judge_response.notes: Coverage is moderate: of 7 identified claims, only C1 (Poisson accuracy, tested on a 1D variant rather than the paper's 2D L-shape), C2 (1D Burgers baseline), and C3 (RAR vs uniform on 1D Burgers) were tested; C4 (2D Burgers at Re=5000), C5 (Lorenz inverse), C6 (fractional PDEs), and C7 (UX) were not. Agreement on tested claims is reasonable: C1 achieves L2_rel = 7.0e-5 on a smooth Poisson problem, consistent with the paper's qualitative accuracy claim. C2 gives mean L2_rel ~0.16 (best seed 0.047), same order of magnitude as the paper's uniform-sampling curve (~0.1). C3 confirms the direction (RAR mean 0.072 vs uniform 0.089, ~19% improvement, winning 2/3 seeds) but with a much smaller effect than the paper's ~2× gap, and one seed shows RAR essentially tied/worse. The report honestly attributes the smaller gap to Adam-only training (no L-BFGS) and only 3 seeds, and does not test C4-C6 at all, so PARTIAL is the correct verdict.
